title: Intersection restriction is locally invertible after sheafification
statement: Let X be a scheme, W an open of X, and P an arbitrary presheaf of O_X-modules. Let K_W(P)(V)=P(V intersect W), with scalars restricted from V, and let nu_P:P→K_W(P) be the restriction map. The morphism obtained from nu_P by module sheafification and restriction to W is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02FU, local insertion cancellation; Tag 01FM, increasing-tuple convention

proof.text: K_W(nu_P) is invertible because intersecting twice with W equals intersecting once. For a module sheaf M on W, the unit on the underlying presheaf of its direct image is invertible, since the inverse images of V and V intersect W in W coincide. Precomposition with nu_P therefore bijects maps K_W(P)→j_*M with maps P→j_*M: the inverse sends f to K_W(f) followed by the inverse unit on j_*M. Injectivity follows by applying K_W and cancelling K_W(nu_P), then using naturality and the invertible target unit. Use the composite sheafification–restriction adjunction to transfer this bijection to morphisms out of the image of nu_P. The coyoneda isomorphism criterion proves that image invertible.

proof_origin.place: Tag 02FU; explicit presheaf and adjunction adaptation by W2
